terms.gloss: a polygon, a figure with many angles
terms.comment: Greek πολύγωνον; as a noun first in Censorinus (third century). The classical authors use adjectives or a description: Columella’s plūrimum angulōrum fōrma (Col. 5.2.1), multangulus, polygōnius.
Vitruvius’s word, of towers built with many faces.

phrases.latin: Triangulum, quadrātum, hexagōnum: omnēs hae figūrae multōrum angulōrum sunt.
phrases.english: Triangle, square, hexagon: all these figures have many corners.

phrases.latin: Omnis ager aut quadrātus, aut longus, aut cuneātus, aut triquetrus, aut rotundus, aut etiam sēmicirculī, vel arcūs, nōnnumquam etiam plūrimum angulōrum fōrmam exhibet.
phrases.english: Every field is square, or oblong, or wedge-shaped, or three-cornered, or round, or else has the shape of a semicircle or an arc, and sometimes even of a figure with many corners.

sources: Lewis & Short: polygonum · Lewis & Short: multangulus · Lewis & Short: polygonius
